subject: Reporting model fit nicely (similar to summary())?

messages.author: a8144d65f36aaf6a
messages.subject: Reporting model fit nicely (similar to summary())?
parts:
Hi,

Is there a way to nicely report model fit (I mean summary(fit)) to a table, like in a PDF? (Eventually, want to include in Rmarkdown)

I have tried semTable, but I get the following error (that cannot debug):

Error in `.rowNamesDF<-`(x, value = value) :
          duplicate 'row.names' are not allowed

Is there a (more) straightforward way around it?

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Reporting model fit nicely (similar to summary())?
parts:
The estimates of the summary() are just text printed using cat(), so you can't capture that exact look without copy/pasting as text.  But all the information is just from parameterEstimates().  So you could use that to put (a subset of) it into a table, using a function like kable() from the knitr package

Terrence D. Jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Reporting model fit nicely (similar to summary())?
parts:
I've been using semTable for my grad SEM class and it works quite well. It does not handle multilevel sem models (gives errors of duplicate row names, which makes sense given that indicators are often used at both levels) or lavaan.mi models (claims the model fit object isn't a lavaan output object).  Problems are probably on the semTable side--I've asked the developers about incorporating fixes for multilevel SEM but haven't seen that addressed, yet.

I should point out, Terrance, that I'm using the dev version of semTools.  

Joe
